newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end a tad higher on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end a tad higher on short-covering.

text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended slightly higher on Tuesday due to short-covering triggered by the yen's surge versus the dollar, traders said.

"Those who sold earlier on reports that the ruling party would make a recommendation (to the prime minister) to raise the official discount rate, moved to buy back when the yen later surged against the dollar," a trader for a city bank's securities unit said.
The June ended at 124.50, up slightly from Monday's close of 124.40. Turnover was 54,942 contracts.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.475 percent as of 0641 GMT, up from Monday's close of 2.460 percent.

NHK television reported early on Tuesday that the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) will make a recommendation to Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto by the end of this month that Japan raise its official discount rate,

An LDP official later said that the ruling party has not yet decided whether to request a raise in the nation's official discount rate as part of a proposal to rationalise government-affiliated financial institutions.

"It is true that the committee is talking about requesting a rise in the official discount rate, but we are still in the process of wrapping it up and have not decided whether to include it in the proposals or not," the official said.
The NHK report had only a limited impact on JGBs, since even if the LDP did make such a request it was unlikely the Bank of Japan would immediately raise rates, traders said.
The Finance Minister said that monetary policy is up to the BOJ, and that seemed to quell market jitters, the trader for a city bank's securities unit said.
Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Tuesday: "Interest rate decisions are up to the Bank of Japan. It is as the BOJ governor has been saying in parliament."
Traders said JGBs were also supported by firmness in long-term cash JGBs.
"City banks have been buying cash JGBs from the 190th to 195th JGBs since yesterday. Such buying seems to be taking place today as well," said a trader with another city bank's securities unit.
The BOJ's monthly report released on Tuesday had little impact on JGBs, traders said.

"The economy is basically on a gradual recovery trend and private demand is becoming firmer, although it is accompanied by fluctuations arising from an increase in the national consumption tax," the report said.
The market will be keeping close tabs on the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting to take place later on Tuesday and a 10-year JGB auction on Wednesday, traders said.
If U.S. interest rates are raised at the FOMC, it could lead to some selling of JGBs, but players will probably be eager to buy on dips, the first trader said.
